clue.text: Kick-off for Spurs after attack goes in

indicators.note: after says the attack piece comes first, with the Spurs letter following it

parts.note: an attack of illness or temper is a fit

indicators.note: the kick-off is the start, so take the opening letter of Spurs

explanation.surface: A football report: Tottenham score straight from the restart after a spell of pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club; here it just supplies its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that goes in a space is said to fit there, so the verb forms are synonyms.

clue.text: Maybe Guy's house is mine, all bar the contents

parts.note: is shortened to 's, as in it's
a pit is a coal mine

indicators.note: everything except the inside letters of all is kept, leaving its two ends

explanation.surface: Someone named Guy claims his house is a mine of everything except what is in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy's is a famous London teaching hospital; 'Maybe' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy's in London is one example of a medical institution where patients are treated.

clue.text: Not such a bright flash a few hours drive from Etna

definitions.text: a few hours drive from Etna

parts.note: a colour that is less bright is paler
in a flash means in a mo, a moment

explanation.surface: A dimmer flash of light seen a few hours' drive from the volcano.
explanation.walkthrough: MO is British slang for a moment, as in 'half a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian capital lies on the island's north coast, some hours by road from the volcano on the east side.

clue.text: Funny story about English native enjoyed by the carpenter?

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go round the English piece
funny suggests something odd, so the letters of story are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An amusing tale about an English local who was enjoyed by a carpenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' turns STORY into OYSTR, and 'about' puts E inside it. In Lewis Carroll's poem 'The Walrus and the Carpenter' the pair eat the young oysters.
explanation.definitionFit: A native is a British term for an oyster raised in local beds, and Carroll's Carpenter eats them.

clue.text: Bright copper keeping head down during 40 day trial period

indicators.note: during says the moved copper letters sit within the Lent piece

parts.note: Lent is the forty days of fasting before Easter

indicators.note: the head letter of the copper symbol is moved down to the end

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A clever policeman keeps a low profile during his forty-day probation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' reads as a policeman but is the metal; in 'keeping head down' its first letter drops to the bottom of this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: This rather literary adjective means giving off light or shining, so it is a synonym of bright.

clue.text: Stinking piece of chicken, maybe time for the bin?

indicators.note: sending something to the bin throws it away, so the time letter is removed

parts.note: a thigh is a cut of chicken, one example

explanation.surface: A smelly bit of chicken: perhaps it's time to throw it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat or game that has gone off is described as high when it smells strongly.

clue.text: Exiles observed returning quietly over Russia's borders

indicators.note: returning means the word for observed is read backwards

parts.note: to observe is to remark or say, past tense said
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its outer letters, first and last

explanation.surface: Exiles were seen coming back quietly across the Russian frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns SAID into DIAS; Russia's borders are its first and last letters, R and A.
explanation.definitionFit: The collective word for a people scattered far from their homeland, so it names a body of exiles.

clue.text: Being unselfish, mum gets a token of love

parts.note: mum, as in keep mum, means be quiet: sh
a ring is given as a token of love

explanation.surface: Mother is generous and receives a love token.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like mother, but it means silent, hence SH.
explanation.definitionFit: Splitting what you have with others is a generous, giving act, so the participles match.

clue.text: I quit that entertaining university women's group

indicators.note: entertaining means holding a guest, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: yon is an old word for that, as in yon hill
the WI is the Women's Institute

explanation.surface: Someone resigns from a group of university women that they found amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute is a British community organisation for women.
explanation.definitionFit: Conceding defeat in an argument or game is the same as saying you surrender.

clue.text: Campers must move — tent's beginning to fall off a cliff

indicators.note: letters that move are rearranged, so this signals a mixing of the fodder

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the opening letter of the tent word is lost

parts.note: the word tent, possessive aside

explanation.surface: Campers have to shift their tent, which is starting to slip off a cliff edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to fall off' drops T from TENT, leaving ENT, and 'must move' rearranges CAMPERS with ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A long steep slope or rock face, such as the edge of a plateau, is a type of cliff.

clue.text: Some of the chosen live on in audio

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some of the elect go on living through recordings.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverberation keeps a sound going after it was made, so it lives on in sound.

clue.text: Office worker's formal attire wasted on the phone

indicators.note: on the phone we only hear words, so the pieces are taken by sound

parts.note: a tie is part of formal dress; wasted is slang for drunk, as is pissed in British use

explanation.surface: An office worker's smart clothes get ruined during a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pissed' is British slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone employed to type letters and documents was a classic clerical job.

clue.text: Philistine always knocked over? Goliath finally ducks

indicators.note: knocked over means turned upside down, so the word for always is reversed in this down clue

parts.note: ay is a poetic word for always

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of Goliath

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O; two of them make OO

explanation.surface: The Philistine giant Goliath always gets knocked down and ends up ducking.
explanation.definitionFit: A boorish, uncultured lout is called a philistine; Swift's brutish creatures gave us the word.

clue.text: Virgin loses virginity at last; one occasion involving sailors

indicators.note: loses says a letter is dropped from the Virgin's name

parts.note: the Virgin is Mary, mother of Jesus

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of virginity

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
time as in one time, an occasion

explanation.surface: A virgin finally loses her virginity, on one occasion with sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: MARY loses Y, the last letter of 'virginity', leaving MAR.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective describes things connected with the sea, seafaring and those who sail.

clue.text: Current business partner of Goldman reported a hacker

indicators.note: reported means said out loud, so the pieces are taken by their sound

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current; Goldman Sachs is the investment bank founded by Goldman and his partner Sachs

explanation.surface: A current business partner of Goldman was said to be a hacker.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken together, I and SACHS say 'eye-sacks', near enough the climber's tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A climber's tool for cutting steps in glaciers chops away at ice, so it is literally a hacker.

clue.text: Much trouble accompanies married crushes

indicators.note: accompanies says the two pieces go along together, side by side

parts.note: ills are troubles, plural for much

explanation.surface: Married life brings lots of trouble and crushing blows.
explanation.definitionFit: To grind grain or pepper is to crush it, so the verbs agree as third-person forms.

clue.text: Jewish artist needs tea and chutzpah

parts.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea
chutzpah is cheek or nerve, also called gall

explanation.surface: A Jewish painter needs a cup of tea and some nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc of that name was a Russian-French painter from a Hasidic family in Belarus.

clue.text: See 15
Without others coming over, a little trifle's enough

indicators.note: coming over says the hidden letters are read backwards
a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Alone, with no guests arriving, a small portion of trifle will do.
explanation.walkthrough: A trifle is a British layered pudding of sponge, custard and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something by yourself, with nobody else, is doing it on your own.

clue.text: 12 running back and forth, drink going to and fro

indicators.note: back says the word for running is read in reverse

parts.note: a machine that is running is on
forth means onward, as in from this day forth, so on
the drink is slang for the sea, and its tide flows in and out

explanation.surface: At noon someone runs back and forth while their drink sloshes about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back and forth' gives NO then ON; the sea's ebb and flow is the tide.
explanation.definitionFit: The old poetic word for midday names the hour when the clock shows twelve.

clue.text: Large, top-quality mushrooms served up in dish of the day

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: L is the clothing abbreviation for large
A1 means first-rate, written AI
ceps are porcini mushrooms

explanation.surface: A big plate of first-class mushrooms is brought out as the restaurant's daily dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reverses the whole string LAICEPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant's dish of the day is listed on the menu as today's special offering.

clue.text: Numb doctor upset with Friday's case

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a case is the outside of something, so the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A doctor, upset and dazed, carries his Friday case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like the medic but is the anagram signal; Friday's case is its first and last letters, F and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To dull the senses or stun someone is a verb that matches the transitive sense of numb.

clue.text: Check work you did mostly in court

indicators.note: in says the middle pieces sit inside the court letters

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
ye is an old word for you

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of did is kept

explanation.surface: Checking up on what you mostly did while in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To review a text for errors before printing is one kind of checking.

clue.text: Herb's 27 inch racket?

parts.note: 27 inches is three quarters of a yard, so three quarters of the word yard
a row is a noisy racket

explanation.surface: A herb's 27-inch racket, presumably for an outsize game of tennis.
explanation.walkthrough: A yard is 36 inches, so 27 inches is three-quarters of it: the first three letters of YARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Achillea, a feathery-leaved plant used in folk medicine, is a common herb.

clue.text: Supernatural presence moaned when disturbed

indicators.note: disturbing things puts them out of place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A ghost moaned when someone disturbed it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this is a spirit or demigod, an invisible being from beyond nature.

clue.text: Port does badly when in recession

indicators.note: badly done means messed up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in recession means going backwards, so the word for when is reversed

parts.note: as means when, as in as I left

explanation.surface: A harbour town struggles during an economic downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' turns DOES into ODES; 'in recession' turns AS into SA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ukrainian city on the Black Sea is a major harbour.

clue.text: West end of soccer pitch is fans' favourite

indicators.note: in an across answer the west end is the left, the first letter

parts.note: pitch is black tar

explanation.surface: The supporters' best-loved player plays at the west end of the football ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' looks like the playing field but is the black sticky substance.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity or leading player loved by supporters is the top performer.

clue.text: Metal point

parts.note: tin is a metal
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a prong of a fork or antler, and its two words also build it.
explanation.definitionFit: A prong of a fork, a sharp metal spike, is exactly a pointed tip of metal.

clue.text: Order Peter a taxi to drive from home

indicators.note: ordering puts things into a new arrangement, so these letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Call Peter a cab to take him away from his house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive' is not a car ride but the verb to force out.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to banish or exile someone from their native country.

clue.text: Performer runs through short musical piece

indicators.note: through says the runs letter goes into the shortened tune
short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a tune is a short piece of music
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A performer runs through a brief song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts TUNE to TUN.
explanation.definitionFit: In variety and music hall an act or entertainer on the bill is called a turn.

clue.text: Completely fascinated by Hebraic books, written from right to left

parts.note: being into something means keen on it

indicators.note: Hebrew is written right to left, so these letters are reversed

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, the Hebrew scriptures

explanation.surface: Totally absorbed by Hebrew texts, which run right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase means as a whole, entirely.

clue.text: 15 18 30, 6 1, two 4 18, 8, 16 28 and 13 25 9 sounded divine among scrapers

indicators.note: among says the divine letters go inside the scrapers

parts.note: filers scrape away with files
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a divine

explanation.surface: A roll-call of puzzle answers that, spoken aloud, sound like holy men among scrapers.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud the cross-referenced answers give violinists: Isaac Stern, Heifetz, the two Oistrakhs, Szeryng, Milstein and Yehudi Menuhin. 'scrapers' is also a jibe at violinists.
explanation.definitionFit: The listed great violinists are all players of the violin, informally called fiddles.
